question: Does native hotjoin send and restore a game snapshot, and which completion, admission and command-reentry boundaries are actually established?

scope.boundary: Static snapshot production, transfer queue, received-stream restoration and guarded control continuation. Fresh disconnected-player admission, slot/XUID reassignment, successful runtime recovery and complete command reconciliation remain open.
scope.hotjoinOwner: U32[0x8314EFDC], abbreviated H; indexed progress map +0x4, separate indexed control map +0x2C, deferred received-transfer ID +0x54.
scope.networkOwner: U32[0x8314EFE0], abbreviated M; +0x10 resolves the service, while +0x44 holds a distinct listener object.
scope.servicePremise: Resolved live service uses vptr 0x8215FA78. Its +0x104 slot at 0x8215FB7C is 0x8222DE40, returning service +0x28, the bulk manager. Its +0x10 listener must be the matching initialized listener; neither numeric registry keys nor an initialized table prove runtime lifetime.
scope.headerPremise: Static game-header object 0x8314F76C uses vptr 0x82138768; +0x6C selects 0x82D81560 and +0x5C selects 0x82D86400. These initialized relations require the retained live vptr at dispatch.

dependencies.use: Indexed reader/writer, removal tail, five-word command record, local queue and numeric turn request.
Conditional header transfer of current main RNG state; no complete RNG or draw-counter restoration claim.
RVA-F-0362 header-backed PE Exception directory and descriptor interpretation.

snapshotProducer.selection: Scans eight indexed entries; a non-sentinel state-one entry selects a transfer attempt. A native memory stream rooted at stack +0x80 uses vptr 0x82136B28.
snapshotProducer.writer: The call at 0x82D90064 selects game-header virtual +0x6C -> 0x82D81560. That owner calls shared header codec 0x82CC29B8 with mode zero at 0x82D815E0, shared body codec 0x82CC4040 with mode zero at 0x82D81654, and compression 0x82D91EF8 at 0x82D8168C. It writes length words and compressed body bytes to the output stream.
snapshotProducer.transfer: 0x82D90084 is a callsite, not a function entry. It calls 0x82D8CB28(M, stream, index), then 0x82D90094 calls 0x82D8F800(H,index,2) without testing the preceding result. The writer result is also not used as a success gate here.
snapshotProducer.shape: A native save-style header and compressed game-body snapshot, using the ordinary save/load codecs. This is implemented world-state transfer, distinct from lobby settings or the five-word command object. It is not raw process memory or a complete host-side runtime snapshot.
snapshotProducer.qualification: A normal nonzero 0x82D8FF78 result establishes that at least one attempt was issued, not that serialization, delivery, peer restore or resumed play succeeded. All native serialized fields and their exclusions are not exhaustively inventoried here.

queueOutcome.explicitFailure: Returns -1 when M +0x10 is null or the first service virtual +0x104 result is null. The service is queried again on the normal arm; that second result is not separately checked before 0x82E65BF8 at 0x82D8CB88.
queueOutcome.normalResult: 0x82E65BF8 creates or finds an 84-byte per-index queue record and calls 0x82E658A8. The latter creates a 52-byte transfer through 0x82CA2640, appends it and returns transfer +0x10 at 0x82E6590C. With the constructor's retained resolved-registry premise, this is a transfer identifier, not a boolean or HRESULT. A null constructor registry lookup skips the ID store; this path does not establish a valid ID result.
queueOutcome.ownedBytes: 0x82CA2640 reads input stream virtual +0x34 size and +0x38 data, copies bytes into owned storage at transfer +0x30, stores length at +0x20 and computes a check word at +0xC. Base 0x82CA2290 initializes internal state +0x14 to zero and stores the +0x10 ID at 0x82CA2310 only after its registry lookup resolves; the null branch at 0x82CA22E4 skips that store.
queueOutcome.callerEffects: Both explicit -1 and normal transfer-ID returns reach the same indexed state-two write. Allocation-null arms can fault rather than return a defined failure result; do not invent a complete error enum or treat every nonpositive result as failure.
queueOutcome.qualification: No-queue failure, successful enqueue, completed send and successful received restore are separate events. ID uniqueness/wrap and all allocation/lifetime invariants are not closed.

sendStates.effect: Builds begin object class 1150 through 0x82CAEC30, then selects internal state one.
Wait state. Request class 1151 consumer 0x82CAEBC8 -> 0x82E65B88 -> 0x82E657F0 changes the matching ID to state two.
Sends class 1152 with ID/length and selects state three.
Constructs class 1153 chunks through 0x82CAE338, at most 1024 bytes each; advances offset/counter and selects three or four.
Runs a completion callback and selects terminal state five. Failure/cancellation can select six.

bulkProtocol.sendCompletion: 0x82E65F08 services the queue through 0x82E65CE8 at 0x82E65F3C. Nonterminal transfers are requeued. Terminal five emits class 1154 with ID/check word; terminal six emits 1155. At 0x82E65ED0 service +0x10 listener virtual +0x50 receives registry key r4, transfer ID r5, player index r6, and success r7=(state==5), before transfer disposal.
bulkProtocol.beginReceive: Begin table 0x8215F588 +0x10 -> 0x82CABDB8 resolves the service and calls listener +0x54. Initialized listener 0x82137570 +0x54 -> 0x82D89AE0 -> 0x82D8C9B8 -> 0x82E65928 creates an owned memory stream indexed by transfer ID in the bulk manager's +0x54 map, with separate kind value two at +0x2C. Admission, callbacks and allocation remain guarded.
bulkProtocol.chunkReceive: Chunk table 0x8215F5C4 +0x10 -> 0x82CAE0E0 obtains the bulk manager through service +0x104 and calls 0x82E64CC0 at 0x82CAE140, with r4=ID from object +0x34, r5=data pointer from +0x44, r6=length from +0x38. 0x82E64CC0 looks up 0x82E64AD0(ID), invokes stream +0x8 with length/data, compares the written count to length, and removes the stream through 0x82E64BB0 on failure.
bulkProtocol.receiveCompletion: Class-1154 table 0x8215F5D8 +0x10 -> 0x82CAF480 calls 0x82E660C0 at 0x82CAF4E0 with ID, source index and check word. That helper requires a matching stream, distinguishes kind one/two, conditionally checks the nonzero supplied check word, finalizes the stream and calls service +0x10 listener +0x58 at 0x82E66228 with r5=ID, r6=source index, r7=success. Table slot 0x821375C8 -> 0x82D895B8 writes r5 into H +0x54 only when low8(r7) is nonzero.
bulkProtocol.replyAndFailure: 0x82CAF480 replies with class 1156 carrying the completion boolean. Class-1155 consumer 0x82CACB58 calls 0x82E64A68, notifying the same listener +0x58 with false. Class-1156 table 0x82137398 +0x10 -> 0x82CAEB58 acts on a false reply through 0x82E65B18; a true reply is not proof that 0x82D86400 ran successfully. Chunk-write failure also sends class 1156 false.
bulkProtocol.qualification: Bulk states zero through six differ from indexed hotjoin progress zero through four. Initialized tables, decoded object class, matching service/ID, routing, listener installation and normal returns are runtime premises. Sender terminal five is not remote-load acknowledgement. No complete GT2 packet grammar, delivery, retry/timeout guarantee or all-peer barrier is established.

restore.entry: 0x82D217C8 reads H +0x54 and, on its nonnegative branch, calls 0x82D8F9A0 at 0x82D21AC4 before continuing setup.
restore.lookup: 0x82D8F9A0 calls 0x82D8B1D0(M,ID), which obtains the bulk manager and calls 0x82E64AD0. For a nonnull returned stream, 0x82D8FA00 dispatches the static game-header virtual +0x5C -> 0x82D86400, with r4=stream, r5=1, r6=0, r7=-1, r8=0.
restore.sharedLoader: 0x82D86400 calls 0x82CC29B8 mode one at 0x82D8645C and, after its header/content/stream guards, 0x82CC4040 mode one at 0x82D86674. These are the same codecs used by snapshot writing, with opposite modes. The loader contains resume/RNG/turn continuation, including 0x82DADC88 and 0x82D7F550. Ordinary file loading instead reaches this loader through outer 0x82D84238.
restore.cleanup: 0x82D8F9A0 does not test the loader result. It calls 0x82D8B5F0 -> 0x82E64BB0, clears H +0x54 to -1, and writes local indexed progress zero through 0x82D8F800. Cleanup also runs when ID lookup is empty; cleared state is not successful load.
restore.qualification: Native received-stream restoration is positively implemented. Header/content/stream rejection, missing stream and loader failure remain distinct. The body codec's raw r3 return is not assigned success/failure semantics and is not tested by this loader. Complete field coverage, pending-command treatment, replay cutoff, world replacement generation and accepted player-facing resume remain open.

receiveToCommand.callback: 0x82CA0798 initializes network callbacks including 0x82C9FB38. With retained connection user data and owner/listener, 0x82C9FB38 invokes listener +0x10 at 0x82C9FB90. Listener vptr 0x821600AC +0x10 -> 0x82CA0B58; 0x82CA5E80 installs this table in service +0x18 and 0x82CA73D8 passes it to network construction.
receiveToCommand.decode: 0x82CA0B58 calls 0x82CB2318 -> 0x82CB20E8, which wraps/reads the received bytes and uses factory 0x82E7DB10 followed by object reader +0xC. A nonnull decoded object reaches service +0xDC -> 0x82CA58A0.
receiveToCommand.routing: After its routing/record/filter branches, 0x82CA58A0 can call service +0xE0 -> 0x82CA4AE8. That helper sends class >=1000 directly to 0x82CB1B28; lower classes require listener +0x4C -> 0x82D895D8 -> 0x82CB1B28.

If the decoded object uses accepted command vptr 0x821368E0, +0x10 -> 0x82D91C58 -> 0x82CE16C8(object+0x34). The queue helper appends the five-word record only when its first word is not -1; -1 only drains existing queued records. Drain dispatches through 0x82CDDF08.
receiveToCommand.qualification: This joins an actual installed receive-callback corridor to conditional local command append. Live factory registration/class/vptr, routing guards, association identity and delivery are premises, not observed facts. It does not close the leading-value-77 factory-registration question or a complete wire, sequence, duplicate-suppression or recovery-queue policy.

conclusion: Native hotjoin includes a compressed save-style transfer, receiver stream writes, completion notification, deferred shared mode-one load and guarded turn-request continuation. A new save-stream transfer feature is not required to explain this native recovery path. Static evidence does not establish successful disconnected-player rejoin, a complete admission protocol, or any particular observed failure cause. Title-specific restore policy and SDK reachability require their own source/runtime evidence.

nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.scope: Selected installed connection callback, service descriptor/index allocation and disconnect-forwarding paths. This binds a native connection-index structure, not the game civilization/player slot or fresh association/XUID admission.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.callback: With the accepted listener and retained registry/service/vptr premises, 0x82CA0BD0 resolves the service using listener+4. Service vptr 0x8215FA78 slot+0x100 at 0x8215FB78 -> 0x82A73340 returns U32[service+0x20], descriptor pointer D. The branch D+8 != -1 and D+8 == D+0x0C takes the selected allocation path. Other branches retain their status/event guards.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.parsedRecord: When incoming r6/r7 are nonzero, the callback requests 160 bytes and calls 0x82CB15B0 only for a nonnull allocation. It then passes the allocated-or-null R and a constructed buffer object to 0x82CB1A58. Those effects are expanded in nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary; this earlier packet establishes only the call edge. With nonnull R it constructs a stack temporary from R+0x5C through 0x821B1500 at 0x82CA0CDC. The service+0x10 listener virtual+0x10 at 0x82CA0CF8 receives the registry key in r4 and that temporary in r5; its return supplies candidate index r26. The temporary is immediately cleaned through 0x821B15C0 at 0x82CA0D04 after the return is retained. Without that nonnull-R branch the candidate remains -1. Payload identity and the listener-to-XUID/player binding are not closed here. No allocation or parser return is assigned an invented failure result.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.allocationEdge: At 0x82CA0D28 the callback calls 0x82CAA360(D,connection,R,candidate). The helper independently resolves a service using D+4, whereas the callback used listener+4. Equality of those keys, returned service and retained lifetime is a premise, not proved by the two lookups. For the helper's actual resolved service it calls virtual+0x148 with R. With selected table 0x8215FA78, +0x148 at 0x8215FBC0 -> 0x82CA3D38. A missing service or zero validation low byte returns -1.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.validation: 0x82CA3D38 defaults to one when service virtual+0x10C returns null. Otherwise it calls that owner's virtual+0x20 with the record, retains the result, conditionally notifies service virtual+0x110 owner's +0x64, and returns the retained result. Owner installation, validation semantics, callback effects and normal returns remain premises; the default-one branch is not proof of an authenticated peer.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.indexSelection: For negative candidate, 0x82CAA360 scans indices zero through seven using 0x82CA9810(D,index) and chooses the first missing record; eight occupied indices return -1. A nonnegative candidate bypasses this free-index scan. No local upper-bound or vacancy rejection for that supplied candidate is proved. These are native connection indices, not newly named civilization slots.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.recordLookup: 0x82CA9810 searches descriptor map at D+0x1C, compares its returned node with D+0x24 sentinel and returns node+0x0C's pointer or zero. This selected lookup does not itself retire an old record. Before the later replacement, 0x82CAA360 calls this lookup with the chosen index and does not retain its result.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.publication: The helper requests a 36-byte record. Under valid allocation/virtual-call/normal-return premises, it writes incoming or conditionally normalized connection at record+0x14, chosen index at +0x18, and passes R through record virtual+4. It conditionally publishes into a connection-keyed D+0x44 map, then 0x82CAA584 obtains the chosen D+0x1C entry and 0x82CAA598 writes the new record pointer there. Existing-record retirement and the connection-normalizing predicate 0x82E46518 remain separate frontier questions, not an inferred leak or rejoin guarantee.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.continuation: After index publication the helper calls service virtual+0x160 with index/R, calls service virtual+0xCC with the chosen index, and invokes virtual+0x16C(index,0) only when that predicate's returned low byte is zero. It then calls service+0x10 listener+0x20 with the registry key/index. Its selected final return is the chosen index. The outer callback treats a nonnegative return as its accepted index branch and emits guarded native object/control notifications; this does not prove a gameplay turn, XSession member update or civilization admission.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.disconnect: 0x82C9FF68 looks up the connection in the separate global registry map, and only its found branch conditionally calls listener+0x18 before two cleanup helpers. For selected listener 0x821600AC, slot+0x18 at 0x821600C4 -> 0x82CA08D8. That helper resolves service, gets D through +0x100, calls 0x82CA97A8(D,connection), then passes its result to service virtual+0x64. Actual removal, XSession leave, callback installation/lifetime and title-generation effects remain open.
nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.userData: 0x82C9FAD0 uses the connection as key into the separate global map at 0x83155F6C; a non-sentinel node returns its +0x0C value, otherwise zero. Installed network callbacks require this retained object/listener join. This is not the relay peer/XUID or game-slot mapping.

nativeConnectionIndexBoundary.loggingProposal: Default-off metadata at existing CA0CF8/CA0CFC resolver call/return, CA0D28/CA0D2C allocation call/return, CAA3B0/CAA3B4 validation, CAA43C/CAA440 existing-record lookup call/return, CAA598 pre-store operands, CAA59C post-store publication and CA0918/CA091C disconnect lookup return. unrunCases: Missing service and validation false return -1; no successful index publication is claimed.

With an existing service, nonzero validation low byte and normal lookup returns, a negative candidate with empty/partly occupied indices selects the first hole in zero..seven; eight occupied indices returns -1.
A supported explicit index is traced separately from free allocation; capture old/new record and both maps before deciding its reuse/retirement policy.
Disconnect missing/found registry and listener branches are distinguished from actual service removal, SDK leave and later rejoin.
Same/new returning XUID and fresh association require an independently proved resolver binding, command cutoff and post-restore turn receipt; no run was performed.

nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.scope: Selected parsed member record, installed listener index resolver, connection occupancy and record-copy callbacks. This extends nativeConnectionIndexBoundary without equating its connection index to a civilization/player or authenticated XUID.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.reader: 0x82CB1A58 passes stream virtual+4 a 36-byte read into R, requests a U32 transfer through 0x822D93E8 for R+0x24, four eight-byte transfers into +0x28..+0x47, four U32 transfers through that helper into +0x48..+0x57, four bytes into +0x58 and 64 bytes into +0x5C. Completed field contents require the stream implementation to supply those requests. This local function does not test those call returns. Stream implementation, read bounds/failure and upstream payload validation remain distinct premises. The offsets match the F-0243 XSession member-record layout. nativeXSessionMembershipBoundary closes the conditional remote-count/XUID call correspondence, while incoming R+0x48 user-index semantics remain open because the local join consumes Q+4 fields instead. This reader alone authenticates neither.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.initialization: 0x82CB15B0 clears the first 36 bytes and count +0x24, zeros four eight-byte entries +0x28 and four byte entries +0x58, sets four U32 entries +0x48 to -1 and requests a 64-byte zero-fill of +0x5C through 0x827F7BB0. Its fill effects, normal return and protected-state noninterference are premises. Its caller requested 160 bytes; these selected field writes cover 156, without a claim about final padding.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.stringConstruction: At accepted callback call 0x82CA0CDC, 0x821B1500 receives R+0x5C as a C-string source. For nonnull source its loop at 0x821B1534 scans to NUL without a 64-byte field limit, then passes computed length/source to 0x82D3B798. The selected reader's 64-byte read does not itself enforce a terminator. This is a concrete parser-to-string hardening seam under a fully nonterminated field; upstream validation and writer normalization remain active research, not proof of native malformed-peer exposure or an observed fault.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.resolver: For the initialized service+0x10 listener vptr 0x82137570, slot+0x10 at 0x82137580 is 0x82D89610. Its local body does not inspect the registry-key argument r4, but forwards it to D8AA60 before any local overwrite; transitive key-independence requires the selected service accessor, not an arbitrary dynamic target. It reads global M=U32[0x8314EFE0], and returns -1 unless 0x82D8AA60(M)'s low byte is nonzero and U32[U32[U32[0x82FFD624]+0x70]+4] equals two. The latter is the accepted gameplay-state discriminator, not a new ownership proof. On that branch it passes the string temporary to 0x82D8B400. The global-M descriptor Dg used by this selector is obtained separately from callback descriptor Dc. CAA360 receives and uses Dc, then independently resolves its service from Dc+4; it does not obtain a third descriptor. Dg==Dc, retained lifetimes and no intervening occupancy mutation between lookup and publication are explicit premises for transferring selector vacancy to the map later written by CAA360; no atomicity/locking contract is proved. The callback/global/allocation-helper service identity is a separate premise; no such equality is proved here. Normal calls remain required.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.descriptorGuard: 0x82D8AA60 requires M+0x10 service and its virtual+0x100 descriptor, reloading through that slot, then returns one only for descriptor+8 != -1 and descriptor+8 == descriptor+0x0C. The numeric relation is proved; naming it host authority requires the accepted descriptor context and does not establish peer authentication.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.selection: 0x82D8B400 rejects an empty temporary. Before every iteration of both passes it reloads setup and derives a scan count of one, except modes four through six use two when setup+0x118 equals one and four otherwise. A stable setup/mode is required for an unchanged range across iterations/passes. For each index below that count, it skips a nonzero 0x82D8AB00(M,index) result. For a zero lookup result it obtains the setup slot string through 0x82DAD4F8 and compares it with the temporary using 0x827F27B0. That comparator folds ASCII A..Z and returns the byte difference, so a zero result selects the first case-insensitive string match. If no match was found it scans the same range for a zero lookup result whose setup string is empty and selects the first such index; otherwise it returns -1. It does not read R+0x28 XUIDs in this selected selector.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.occupancyAndString: 0x82D8AB00 resolves M+0x10 virtual+0x100 descriptor and returns 0x82CA9810(descriptor,index), or zero on missing service/descriptor; with a retained nonnull service/descriptor the accepted index map supplies occupancy. A zero result can also mean unavailable service/descriptor, so the selector's zero eligibility alone does not prove vacancy. 0x82DAD4F8 searches setup+8 using index and sentinel setup+0x10, returning found node+0x0C's string object or U32[0x8314EFCC]+0xE0's fallback string. These are connection-index/setup-string joins, not fresh proof of game-player or XSession membership.
nativeMemberNameSelectionBoundary.recordCopy: For record vptr 0x8215F834, virtual+4 at 0x8215F838 is 0x82CA9070. Nonnull R causes allocation/initialization of a 160-byte record+0x10 object when absent, then 0x82CB16D8 requests member-record copying into it.
